subject: Dedicated capacity micro-plan: Nimbus pilot allocations & autoscale exception
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, ops@nimbushealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity micro-plan: Nimbus pilot allocations & autoscale exception

Team —

Quick heads-up and ask for coordinated approval/path forward for the Nimbus Health pilot that starts the week of July 8. This is a 3-week pilot (internal QA + limited public beta) to validate low-latency chart summarization for their EMR ingestion pipeline. Key asks:

- Reserve a contiguous dedicated slice equivalent to 8 A100-class GPUs (can be 8xH100/quantized-equivalent for cost mix) for 3 weeks (7/8 — 7/29).
- Temporarily relax the default autoscale trigger for that slice to allow sustained throughput for 90m windows (our typical hard cap will preempt it otherwise). We need the slice to remain available for steady inference bursts tied to Nimbus’ scheduled data pushes.
- Keep fallback routing enabled to send overflow to the shared burst pool (we’ll accept higher token costs if needed).

Why this matters: Nimbus is a near-term sales opportunity (see SLA ask attached) — they need consistent latency (p95 < 220ms) during the pilot. If we can commit predictable dedicated capacity and an autoscale exception window, they’ll sign an initial month after the pilot. If we can’t, they may look at a competitor who offers guaranteed slices.

Attached: nimbus_pilot_capacity_profile_v1.pdf (workload profile) and pilot_sla_draft.docx.

Asks from each team:
- Kimberly / Product: confirm we can sign the pilot SLA language (latency/availability) and whether we need an explicit product-holder approval.
- Jonas / Infra: can you carve the 8-GPU contiguous slice for the dates (and grant the temporary autoscale exception)? If 8 is not feasible, propose minimum viable allocation.
- Laura / Sales Ops: can you coordinate the MOU and procurement language and create a DED ticket so billing/procurement can reconcile?
- Marcus / Network: confirm any VPC/network prerequisites for the pilot.

I know this is tight — Nimbus is flexible on a minor discount if we can guarantee the runway. Requesting a short sync tomorrow 10:30am PT if that helps.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity micro-plan: Nimbus pilot allocations & autoscale exception

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary and the artifacts. High level: product is supportive but we need to be explicit about two items before signing an SLA:

1) Quality regression clause — Pilots must include a short prompt/regression suite that we can run pre- and post-deploy. That needs to be in the MOU so we can surface quality alerts.
2) Fallback behavior — If the dedicated slice is preempted, what is the acceptable degradation for Nimbus? If they expect consistent p95 < 220ms, fallback to shared pool could violate that. We should set an agreed-upon degraded SLA for the fallback path.

Operational question for infra (Jonas): can we make the autoscale exception scoped to the pilot’s slice ID and time window (so it doesn’t inadvertently disable autoscale globally)? We should avoid any policy-level changes that affect other customers.

If a shorter contiguous allocation (6 GPUs) meets latency targets in the attached profile, I’m okay with that as a conservative compromise.

I can draft the regression clause and degraded-fallback language if you want — will share a short text for inclusion in the MOU.

Kimberly Park
Sr. PM, Dedicated Products
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, ops@nimbushealth.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity micro-plan: Nimbus pilot allocations & autoscale exception

Karthik / Kim —

Quick infra readout after looking at current pool commitments for the US-west cluster:

- 8 contiguous A100-equivalent GPUs for the requested window is tight given two concurrent pilots next week. We can do one of the following (ranked):
  1) Allocate a 6-GPU contiguous slice dedicated to Nimbus for 7/8 — 7/29 and auto-provision an additional 2 GPUs from the burst pool during scheduled push windows (we can reserve burst buffer ahead of time to reduce preemption risk).
  2) If Nimbus insists on 8 dedicated GPUs, we can accommodate by temporarily shifting one non-critical internal slate to another region (requires NAT/VPC prep time ~48h and Marcus support).
  3) Grant a scoped autoscale exception that allows the Nimbus slice to hold for 90m sustained windows, but we need a written emergency rollback trigger and on-call contact.

Operational constraints: autoscale exceptions are scoped to slice IDs and timeboxes — we won’t change global policy. We’ll need an internal DED change with explicit start/end times and a manual rollback plan. I can create the infra change ticket (DED-1423) and set the slice guardrails.

Marcus — can you confirm the VPC peering / ingress limits if we choose option #2?

Jonas Weber
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, ops@nimbushealth.com, partnerships@cloudpartners.io
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity micro-plan: Nimbus pilot allocations & autoscale exception

All —

Thanks for the rapid responses. Summary and next steps (agreed items):

- Allocation: we will proceed with Jonas’ option #1: a 6-GPU contiguous dedicated slice for 7/8 — 7/29, with 2 GPUs backed from the burst pool on scheduled pushes. Jonas will reserve that burst buffer to reduce preemption risk.
- Autoscale exception: scoped to the Nimbus slice ID and the pilot window; infra (Jonas) will create DED-1423 and include an emergency rollback trigger plus on-call owner.
- Product asks: Kimberly to draft the regression suite clause + degraded-fallback SLA language by Monday 7/2 EOD. Kimberly, please include the exact degraded p95 acceptance criteria for fallback routing.
- Procurement / MOU: I’ll open a Billing/Procurement ticket and attach the pilot_sla_draft.docx and Kim’s clause. Ops (Nimbus) — please confirm acceptance of the 6+2 model and that the pilot start date can remain 7/8.
- Network: Marcus to confirm whether cross-region shift (option #2) is needed as contingency and list any VPC steps.

Action owners and deadlines:
- Jonas: create DED ticket + reserve burst buffer (DED-1423) — due 7/1 10am PT
- Kimberly: regression clause + fallback SLA text — due 7/2 EOD
- Laura: open procurement ticket and draft MOU update — due 7/1 5pm PT
- Marcus: VPC checklist / contingency report — due 7/1 2pm PT
- Karthik: confirm with Nimbus and CloudPartners on the 6+2 plan and discount language — please confirm by 7/1 noon PT

If everyone is aligned I’ll mark this as approved for proceeding and post the DED ticket link here once Jonas creates it.

Thanks — let’s keep this tight; Nimbus is expecting the runway.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
